about: The drawn width of a gamma-ink version 2 stroke (docs/dev/handwriting.md 'Width'): width = size * w when the stroke carries the w channel, else size; the drawn opacity is opacity * o when it carries o, else opacity. The only width and opacity laws are the client's finishStroke.js brush table (BRUSHES, bakeWidths), run once when a stroke is finished and again when a selection's brush is restyled; the server and every renderer read w and o. From milestone 3 the w channel's running sum is checked to 0..4000 (decoded 0..4.000; the pencil reaches 3.5) and the o channel to 0..1000. Two row shapes. A SINGLE-SAMPLE row gives a stroke's style (tool, brush, pen, and shape, the stroke's shape record, when the row has one), its size, one sample's decoded pressure p (0..1) and altitude a (degrees or null) and expects: w_enc, the integer written to the first sample's w slot (the multiplier times 1000), w, the decoded multiplier (null when the style writes no w channel), width, the drawn diameter in points, and, when the row has them, o_enc / o, the opacity multiplier the same way (null when the style writes no o channel). frontend/tests/finishStroke.test.mjs runs bakeWidths on the one sample and checks encodeStroke / decodeStroke, strokeWidth and strokeOpacity give w, o, width; backend/tests/test_shared_fixtures.py builds the stroke with w_enc (and o_enc) in its pts, or without the channels, and checks stroke_polyline gives width and decode_stroke gives o. A MULTI-SAMPLE row has `samples`, the whole stroke as [x, y, p | null, t, a | null] (page points, pressure, ms, altitude; azimuth is never read by a width law), `ws`, the baked multiplier per sample to three decimals (and `os` for the pencil), `w_encs`, the integers the w slots hold (absolute, then deltas), both null when the style writes no w channel, and `at` / `w` / `width` for one sample of it as above. The node test bakes the samples with bakeWidths and checks ws / os (within 0.0005) and w_encs, or that nothing is baked; the Python test encodes the samples with ws (and os) through encode_points, or without a w channel, and checks that stroke_polyline's widths are size * ws (the size at every sample without ws) and that the sample at `at` decodes to w. The iPad shell's port of the laws, which draws its live line (ipad/GammaIPad/Pencil/InkWidth.swift), is held to every row by ipad/GammaIPadTests/InkWidthTests.swift, the file a resource of its test bundle: InkWidth.widths and InkWidth.opacities on the row's sample (or its samples) give w and o (ws and os, within 0.0005), and nil where the style writes no w or no o channel. LAWS. pen (brush absent): w = 1 + (p - 0.5), perfect-freehand's on-screen value at thinning 0.5, capped to [0, 2]; it ignores a. monoline ('Ballpoint'), a highlighter and a pen:false Pen or Ballpoint stroke: no w. brush ('Brush'): w = 2p shaped by two tapers over the stroke's arc length L (total T) - a start taper of S = min(2 * size, T / 2), ts = easeOutSine(L / S) while L < S, else 1; an end taper of E = min(3 * size, T / 2), te = easeOutSine((T - L) / E) while T - L < E, else 1 (each taper at most half the stroke, so a short mark keeps its width in the middle; a stroke of no length, T = 0, has no taper and draws 2p); easeOutSine(x) = sin(x * pi / 2) - w = clamp(2p * min(ts, te), 0.1, 2.0) (the floor is 0.1 * size, the cap 2.0); when the pointer reports no pressure (pen:false, or p absent because the pressure preference is off) p is simulated from the spacing of consecutive samples, in page points, with perfect-freehand's simulatePressure step (without its averaging over the first ten points): p0 = 0.5 and, for each later sample at distance d from the one before, sp = min(1, d / size), rp = 1 - sp, p_i = min(1, p_(i-1) + (rp - p_(i-1)) * sp * 0.275); time is not read, so the spacing alone decides. pencil ('Pencil'): w = (1 + (p - 0.5)) * (1 + 2 * (1 - a / 90)) capped to [0, 4] with a defaulting to 90 when the sample has none, and o = clamp(0.15 + 0.85 p, 0, 1) written in the o channel; a pen:false pencil stroke writes neither w nor o. SHAPES: a stroke that carries a shape record (a held shape, a straight highlight, committed pen:false) is constant width whatever its brush: no law runs on it, so it writes neither w nor o, keeps its brush key and is written xyt (a Brush's tapers on a two-sample line would leave both samples at the floor). Every law rounds w and o to three decimals before encoding. The server also refuses a file where size * max(w) > 100.

rows.note: default pen at rest pressure draws the nominal size
default pen at zero pressure draws half
default pen at full pressure draws one and a half
a quarter pressure on a 2 pt pen
the multiplier keeps three decimals
a thin pressure value
the default pen ignores altitude
the default pen ignores altitude at any pressure
the widest stroke the server accepts: size * max(w) <= 100
monoline writes no w and draws its size
a highlighter writes no w and draws its size
a mouse or finger stroke (pen false) writes no w and draws its size
a mouse ballpoint stroke writes no w either
brush: a stroke of one sample (a tap) has no length to taper, so it draws the law's width, 2p, as perfect-freehand draws a lone point at its untapered radius

brush, a short mark, size 2: a 2 pt comma sampled every 0.25 pt every 8 ms at p 0.5; each taper is held to half the mark's length (1 pt), so its middle reaches 2p = 1 and its ends the floor, where the full tapers (4 pt and 6 pt) would keep the whole mark under a third of its width

brush with pressure, size 2: a 20 pt line sampled every 1 pt every 8 ms with p rising 0.2 to 1; the start taper covers the first 4 pt, the end taper the last 6 pt; at 15 pt the line is 2 * 0.8 * easeOutSine(5 / 6) = 1.545 wide, the widest the stroke gets

brush without pressure (a mouse, pen false), size 2: samples 16 ms apart (a 60 Hz mouse) spaced 0.5 pt, then 2 pt, then 0.5 pt; the simulated pressure rises while the pointer is slow (p 0.5 to 0.562 over the first 2 pt) and falls while it is fast (to 0.113 at 12 pt), so the fast middle is thin; the law reads the spacing per sample, never the time, so the same points 1 ms apart bake the same w; the stroke is written with ch xytw (no p)

a stroke that carries a shape record is constant width whatever its brush: a Brush preset's held straight line (pen false, two samples, shape a line) bakes no w and is written xyt, so it draws its size end to end, where the Brush's tapers would put both of its samples at the 0.1 floor and every renderer, interpolating between them, would draw a hairline; its brush key stays
pencil held upright (altitude 90) at rest pressure draws the nominal size at opacity 0.575
pencil at altitude 60 widens by 1 + 2/3
pencil at altitude 30 widens by 1 + 4/3: past the old 2.0 ceiling, which is why the w channel's range is 0..4.000 from milestone 3
pencil at full pressure and altitude 30 reaches the law's widest, 1.5 * 2.333 = 3.5, fully opaque
pencil at full pressure upright: the pen's width, fully opaque
pencil at zero pressure: half the width, the faintest opacity 0.15
pencil at a light slant: 0.7 * 2 = 1.4 wide, opacity 0.15 + 0.17
pencil with no tilt reported: altitude defaults to 90, so only pressure counts
the widest pencil the server accepts: 28.5 * 3.5 = 99.75
a mouse or finger pencil stroke (pen false) is even: no w, no o, the grain alone makes it soft
